money.note: Individuals gave $1,165,399; PAC money $837,451; candidate's own money $0. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Attorney. Born in Philadelphia; Brown University graduate (1985) and UNC law graduate (1990). Served in the North Carolina House of Representatives from 2003 to 2013. Was the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in 2016. Has represented North Carolina's 2nd Congressional District in the U.S. House since January 2021.

endorsements.text: Humane World Action Fund is listed by Ballotpedia as having endorsed Ross in 2026, along with a number of Sway voter-guide groups.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Ross grew up or when she moved to North Carolina. We found no statements from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, land ownership, growth, gun policy, abortion, school choice or policing, and no documented stance on development or data centers. Ballotpedia notes she did not complete its candidate survey in any recent cycle. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties or notable endorsements beyond the voter-guide groups listed. The Ballotpedia page we had was cut off partway through the 117th Congress key votes, so her votes from that period are not covered.

votes.what: Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.

votes.bill: S. 1071 / FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (final)
votes.what: Final FY2026 defense policy and funding-authorization bill (about $900 billion), carried in the House on the vehicle S. 1071.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Nov. 12 final, ended the shutdown)
votes.what: Ended the 43-day federal shutdown: funds government through Jan. 30, 2026 and three full-year spending bills.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Sept. 19 House passage)
votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.bill: H.R. 881 (2025) DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act
votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.
Requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

votes.bill: H.R. 1968 (2025) Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).

votes.bill: H.R. 152 (2025) Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.

cands.name: Eugene F. Douglass
cands.bio: Retired chemistry professor who taught college chemistry for over 30 years, including at UNC Pembroke from 2005. Holds a Ph.D. from North Carolina State University (2010). Republican candidate for NC-2 in 2024 (lost the primary) and 2026. Has held no elected office.
cands.gaps: We found no record of Douglass's birthplace. We found nothing from him on data centers, development or growth, homestead or property taxes, limits on foreign or investor land buying, H-1B or immigration enforcement, policing, gun policy, or school choice and teacher pay. His survey calls generally for lower taxes, a smaller federal government and abolishing the federal Department of Education, but it does not address these topics directly. He has held no office, so there are no official actions to report. The only source available was his Ballotpedia page and survey answers. We found no news coverage, no endorsements, and no controversies.

local.label: Roots 40: He says he grew up in Swarthmore, PA, and has lived in North Carolina since 2005, when he came to teach chemistry at UNCP, so he arrived as an adult about 21 years ago.

qual.background: Taught college chemistry for over 30 years, including at UNC Pembroke, and earned a Ph.D. from NC State in 2010. He has held no elected or governing office and lost the 2024 Republican primary for this seat.

pro-life.evidence: He said he would protect innocent human life from conception until natural death and end abortion for birth control purposes. He would regulate abortion to spare as many lives as possible, and he described partial-birth abortion as unnecessary. This is from his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.
